data.title: Perpetua Resources Announces Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Project Update
data.description:
BOISE, Idaho, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Perpetua Resources Corp. (Nasdaq: PPTA) () ("Perpetua Resources" or "Perpetua" or the "Company") announced the filing of its unaudited condensed consolidated financial results for the period ended September 30, 2026. For details, please see the Company's related filing available on EDGAR and SEDAR+.

"Perpetua made significant progress in Q3 2026," said Jon Cherry, President and CEO of Perpetua Resources. "From advancing temporary and permanent worker housing to pioneering new access into the site, our Stibnite Gold Project is well positioned to move forward with disciplined execution. Our exploration drill program delivered compelling new mineralization, including multiple high-grade gold intervals and a new gold-tungsten discovery."

Webinar Update on Tuesday, November 17, 2026

Perpetua is pleased to announce that it will host a webinar on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, at 9:00 AM Mountain Time (11:00 AM Eastern Time). The webinar will feature members of the executive team and provide an update on project construction and a summary of recent exploration results. The presentation will be followed by a question & answer session. During the webinar, members of the executive team may discuss or disclose material business, financial or operational information that has not been previously publicly disclosed. The webinar may be accessed via telephone using the dial-in information provided below.

Webinar Details:

  • Title: "Perpetua Resources Advancing the Stibnite Gold Project"
  • Date: Tuesday, November 17, 2026
  • Time: 9:00 AM MT / 11:00 AM ET
  • Registration Link:https://us02web.zoom.us/j/81404359572?pwd=rLXP8kzBMsbap4hH6ZTr9Z5pCax5iJ.1 
  • Dial-in Number: +1 (301) 715-8592
  • Meeting ID: 814 0435 9572
  • Passcode: 065330

In addition to the live webinar, the webinar presentation will be posted on Perpetua's website at https://perpetuaresources.com/investors shortly before the webinar begins, and the webinar presentation will be available on Perpetua's website for at least 90 days following the event.

Third Quarter 2026 and Recent Highlights

  • Construction: Worker housing facility civil works were completed in late August 2026, and foundation installation commenced during the quarter. Work on the Burntlog Route ramped up through the summer field season, and long-lead powerline items have been ordered.
  • Exploration: The 2026 Exploration Drilling Program is complete, with more than 16,000 meters of core drilled. In August and then in November 2026, the Company reported new high-grade gold and antimony discoveries and identified a new gold-tungsten zone.
  • Financing update: Perpetua continued diligence and documentation on the $2.9 billion senior secured long-term loan from the Export-Import Bank of the United States ("U.S. EXIM") under the Make More in America Initiative, approved by the U.S. EXIM board on May 21, 2026. Closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027. The Company continues to advance detailed engineering, long-lead procurement, early works, critical path construction, and execution planning ahead of a final investment and construction decision. Unrestricted cash was $443.4 million as of September 30, 2026.
  • Antimony pilot plant: In July 2026, the Company commissioned a mobile modular processing plant, in partnership with Idaho National Laboratory, for pilot-scale testing to advance a secure domestic supply chain for antimony trisulfide.
  • Community: In July 2026, the Company opened a community resource and visitor information center in Yellow Pine, Idaho.

Construction Update

Perpetua completed 494,480 work hours during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, with no reportable spills and no serious injuries. Other highlights include:

  • Burntlog Route: Crews advanced construction along the alignment, removed dead timber left by past wildfires, and moved to pioneer roadwork. The year-round access road will give the Project an expanded and upgraded route capable of handling larger loads and equipment.
  • Worker Housing Facility: Treated wood foundations were installed for the kitchen, dining, and recreation modules, and a metal foundation was installed to support the dormitory buildings and the arctic corridor.
  • Powerline: Perpetua is well advanced in procuring key equipment. Substations and transformers are on order, while deliveries of power poles and ancillary equipment continue to the Company's laydown areas in Donnelly and Cascade, Idaho. Power pole installation commenced in October.

Looking ahead, Perpetua will continue to advance critical path work including bridge deliveries for Burntlog Route, installation of the worker housing facility, ongoing powerline procurement and construction, and placing orders for long-lead-time equipment.

New Exploration Results Announced

The 2026 drilling program sought to upgrade in-pit and near-pit inferred resources, extend mineralization along strike, test key underground targets, and follow up on discoveries from the 2025-2026 program. Recent highlights included:

  • Fiddle Discovery: The new Fiddle prospect, located approximately 750 meters south of the permitted Yellow Pine Pit, includes some of the most significant mineralized material encountered at the Stibnite Gold Project to date. Discovery hole SB633 returned 109.7 meters of 3.2 g/t gold and 1.1% antimony. Fiddle adds a new target area with potential to expand the Project's in-pit and near-pit resource base. The Company has since completed significant additional drilling at Fiddle, with assay results expected in the coming months.
  • Clark Tunnel Fault Zone (CTFZ): First announced in August, the CTFZ is located within or adjacent to the southeastern limits of the permitted Yellow Pine Pit. New results announced earlier this month returned near-surface, high-grade gold intercepts from recent drilling, including 25.4 meters of 4.5 g/t gold from 13 meters downhole and 25.0 meters of 2.3 g/t gold from 18 meters downhole. These results follow the drilling announced in August, which included a tungsten discovery in Hole SB597 that returned 21.3 meters of 3.2 g/t gold and 0.9% tungsten from 24 meters downhole.

Near-Term Outlook

Through the remainder of 2026 and early 2027, Perpetua is advancing early works, critical path construction, and detailed engineering for the process plant. Other initiatives include finalizing key construction and equipment contracts. With the 2026 exploration program recently completed, Perpetua expects to announce ongoing exploration results into 2027.

Website: www.perpetuaresources.com

About Perpetua Resources and the Stibnite Gold ProjectPerpetua Resources Corp., through its wholly owned subsidiaries, is focused on the exploration, site restoration and redevelopment of gold-antimony-silver deposits in the Stibnite-Yellow Pine district of central Idaho. The Stibnite Gold Project is one of the highest-grade, open-pit gold deposits in the United States and holds the only identified domestic reserve of the critical mineral antimony, which is essential to the defense, energy and manufacturing sectors. The Project is designed to apply a modern, responsible mining approach to restore a historic mine site and provide uplift to water quality, improve fish habitat access, and invest in river restoration while supporting local economic development in rural Idaho.

Cautionary Statement Regarding Technical Information

Except for the exploration results referenced herein, the technical information in respect of the Stibnite Gold Project in this news release is based upon information contained in the technical report titled "Stibnite Gold Project, S-K 1300 Technical Report Summary, Valley County, Idaho, USA," dated as of December 31, 2025 (the "TRS"), developed for the Stibnite Gold Project in accordance with the mining property disclosure rules specified in Regulation S-K subpart 1300 ("S-K 1300") promulgated by the SEC and published on March 31, 2026. Such information is as of December 31, 2025 and is subject to the assumptions, exclusions and qualifications set forth in the TRS. For additional information regarding the TRS, investors are encouraged to refer to the Company's Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025, filed with the SEC on March 31, 2026.

Furthermore, development of any additional resources and reserves discovered would be subject to any applicable NEPA and permitting requirements.

Data regarding domestic antimony reserves is based on U.S. Geological Survey, Mineral Commodity Summaries, dated as of January 2026.

Quality Assurance

The exploration activities at the Stibnite Gold Project site were carried out under the supervision of Christopher Morgan, CPG, and Christopher Dail, CPG, both Qualified Persons as defined in NI 43-101 and in S-K 1300.

Samples were handled and shipped via Chain of Custody Procedures. Analyses were carried out by ALS Global Laboratories in their Reno and Elko, Nevada and Vancouver, British Columbia laboratories and by MSA Laboratories in Elko, Nevada and Langley, British Columbia.

All gold assays were determined using photon assay techniques, which include a 0.015 g/t lower reporting limit. Antimony assays were determined using pressed pellet XRF and include a lower reporting limit of 0.04% Sb and an upper reporting limit of 4% Sb. Some intervals may not add or subtract correctly due to rounding, but differences are deemed insignificant.

Umpire samples are routinely submitted to third-party labs and blank and standard samples are inserted at appropriate intervals for quality assurance and quality control. A review of the results of analyses of blanks, standards and duplicates by the Company's Qualified Person indicates values are within normal and acceptable ranges.

data.title: Nvidia Has Real Problems-but Don't Fall For Fear Mongering — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Al Root

While accounting isn't always fun, it's necessary to understand — especially when numbers being thrown around aren't what they seem.

Nvidia stock is floundering in the wake of a scandal that has forced co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang to resign. Among the mountain of challenges the company is facing, investors have plenty to worry about — but the reemergence of accounting risks isn't one of them.

Did you know that Nvidia lists commitments and contingencies totaling $366 billion? And additional commitments of $56 billion? And another $108.5 billion in commitments to OpenAI? That adds up to $530.5 billion, a lot for a company that lists total liabilities on its balance sheet of $91 billion.

Well, yes. Because those figures are disclosed in quarterly filings. What's more, most of that money has little to do with circular financing, where Nvidia supplies money to customers who buy its hardware.

The bulk of that $530.5 billion — some $279 billion — are commitments representing future payment to suppliers such as memory chip makers. The money is disbursed over many years and flows through the income statement, accounting expert Robert Willens says.

Nvidia didn't respond to a request for comment about its accounting. Nvidia stock was down 2.2% in late trading on Friday at $162.56, leaving it down about 13% for the week. The S&P 500 was off 0.5%.

Broadcom reported $127 billion in similar purchase commitments. Its total balance sheet liabilities are $88 billion.

Both Nvidia and Broadcom's purchase committments are rising partly because of the high cost of memory chips.

Neither number is all that concerning, or out of line. Nvidia's chip business is roughly five times the size of Broadcom's.

Nvidia's commitments related to the AI buildout are closer to $200 billion, including more than $100 billion for OpenAI.

That is a lot of money, and circular financing is a risk to consider. But AI data-center hyperscalers are spending trillions, not billions. Most AI financing comes from cash flow, equity issuance, bonds, and loans.

Questions about Nvidia's willingness to extend financing terms to customers are certainly valid. It's just important to have the right numbers. Nvidia's customer finance commitments are closer to $200 billion, not half a trillion.

Write to Al Root at allen.root@dowjones.com

data.title: Tempest Therapeutics Reports Q3 2026 Results, $0.9 Million Cash Balance
data.description:
Tempest Therapeutics reported a third-quarter 2026 net loss of $3.6 million, or $0.21 per share, and ended September with $0.9 million in cash. The company said its cash is expected to fund operating expenses for less than 12 months from the date its financial statements were available to be issued, raising substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern. The quarter’s business update included an exclusive license for Senlang’s CD7-targeted lentiviral in vivo CAR-T platform.

Financial Highlights

  • Third-quarter net loss was $3.6 million, compared with $3.5 million in the year-earlier quarter; net loss per share was $0.21, versus $0.79.
  • For the first nine months of 2026, net loss was $36.6 million, or $2.54 per share, compared with $22.2 million, or $5.71 per share, in the same period of 2025.
  • Cash and cash equivalents totaled $0.9 million at September 30, 2026, down from $7.7 million at December 31, 2025. Cash used in operating activities during the first nine months was $12.4 million.
  • Third-quarter research and development expenses were $0.2 million and general and administrative expenses were $2.6 million. For the first nine months, those expenses were $2.1 million and $11.5 million, respectively, with acquired in-process research and development expenses of $22.2 million.
  • Tempest recorded $0.8 million in third-quarter financing costs related to its Lincoln Park equity line. It also reported approximately $1.8 million in net proceeds from its September private placement and approximately $0.3 million in gross proceeds from Lincoln Park share sales through September 30.

Business Highlights

  • Tempest exercised its option to obtain an exclusive worldwide license, excluding China, to Senlang’s CD7-targeted lentiviral vector platform and associated in vivo CAR-T candidates.
  • Lead candidate TPST-4903, a BCMA/GPRC5D dual-targeting in vivo CAR-T therapy, is being evaluated in a Phase 1 dose-escalation study for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. The company said preliminary clinical responses were encouraging and that initial data are expected at an upcoming scientific conference.
  • Tempest highlighted TPST-4003, a CD19/BCMA dual-targeting candidate using its CD7-targeted mRNA/LNP delivery platform. An investigator-initiated study in China involving approximately 10 patients with myasthenia gravis or multiple sclerosis is expected to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026.
  • The company appointed Nancy Freda-Smith and John W. Frederick as independent directors, citing their corporate governance and capital markets expertise.

data.title: BeyondSpring Reports $50.5 Million Q3 Net Income, Advances DUBLIN-4
data.description:
BeyondSpring reported third-quarter 2026 net income of $50.5 million, largely reflecting a $53.7 million gain on the sale of subsidiary interests, while its continuing operations recorded a $2.1 million net loss. The company reported no revenue and a $2.1 million operating loss for the quarter. Business updates included FDA Fast Track designation for Plinabulin plus docetaxel and a transaction to support China-based enrollment in the DUBLIN-4 trial.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue was $0 for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.
  • Operating loss from continuing operations was $2.1 million for the third quarter, compared with $1.6 million a year earlier; the nine-month operating loss was $5.7 million, versus $5.9 million.
  • Net income was $50.5 million for the third quarter, including a $53.7 million gain on the sale of subsidiary interests. Net income attributable to BeyondSpring was $50.8 million.
  • For the nine months, net income was $38.1 million, including the sale gain; net income attributable to BeyondSpring was $47.8 million.
  • Basic and diluted earnings per share were $1.24 for the quarter, including a $0.05 loss per share from continuing operations. Cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments totaled $0.6 million at September 30, 2026, compared with $4.0 million at December 31, 2025.

Business Highlights

  • The FDA granted Fast Track designation to Plinabulin plus docetaxel for advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC without actionable genomic alterations after anti-PD-(L)1 therapy and platinum-based chemotherapy. The designation may allow more frequent FDA interactions and, if criteria are met, rolling review.
  • BeyondSpring completed the sale of BeyondSpring Ltd., which indirectly held a majority equity interest in Bulin, to Biolin on September 30, 2026. Under the transaction, Biolin will support Bulin’s DUBLIN-4 clinical development activities at participating sites in China, with enrollment expected to include approximately 221 patients.
  • BeyondSpring will have access to clinical data from the China portion of DUBLIN-4. The global Phase 3 trial plans to enroll 442 patients, with a prespecified interim analysis at 221 progression-free survival events.
  • The company cited DUBLIN-3 results and a post-ICI subgroup analysis, along with prospective Phase 2 Study 303 data presented at ASCO 2026, as clinical rationale for evaluating Plinabulin in the post-ICI setting.

data.description:
BCP Investment reported third-quarter 2026 net investment income of $4.6 million, or $0.37 per share, and a net decrease in assets from operations of $13.5 million. Net asset value was $162.7 million, or $13.13 per share, at September 30. The company also agreed to acquire Investcorp Credit Management BDC at consideration equal to 90% of its adjusted net asset value.

Financial Highlights

  • Total investment income was $13.9 million, down from $18.9 million in the third quarter of 2025. Core investment income, excluding purchase discount accretion, was $12.2 million.
  • Net investment income was $4.6 million, or $0.37 per share, compared with $8.8 million, or $0.71 per share, a year earlier.
  • The net decrease in assets resulting from operations was $13.5 million, or $1.09 per share, versus a $23.6 million increase, or $1.88 per share, in the prior-year quarter.
  • Net asset value was $162.7 million, or $13.13 per share, compared with $179.5 million, or $14.49 per share, at June 30, 2026.
  • At quarter-end, investments had a fair value of $434.2 million. Outstanding borrowings were $282.4 million at par, and the asset coverage ratio was approximately 157%.

Business Highlights

  • BCP Investment entered into a merger agreement to acquire Investcorp Credit Management BDC. ICMB shareholders will receive newly issued BCP Investment shares and, if applicable, cash, based on consideration equal to 90% of ICMB’s adjusted net asset value. The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions, including ICMB shareholder approval.
  • During the quarter, the company deployed approximately $3.1 million and received approximately $8.9 million from repayments and sales, resulting in net repayments and sales of approximately $5.8 million.
  • Non-accrual debt investments declined to 10 across seven portfolio companies, from 11 across seven companies in the prior quarter. They represented 2.8% of the portfolio’s fair value and 6.0% of amortized cost.
  • BCP Investment amended its KeyBank revolving credit facility, increasing committed capacity to $150 million, lowering borrowing spreads, and extending the reinvestment period to August 2029 and maturity to August 2031. The amendment consolidated secured revolving borrowings after the JPMorgan facility was repaid and terminated.
  • The company issued an additional $10 million of 7.50% notes due 2029 and redeemed its remaining $10 million of 2026 Notes in October, eliminating that near-term maturity.
  • BCP Investment declared monthly base distributions of $0.09 per share for January, February and March 2027.

data.title: Grades steady as global oil markets set to return to surplus
data.description:
Grades were little changed on Friday, dealers said, even as global oil market was set to return to a surplus in the fourth quarter of this year, according to the International Energy Agency.

Oil supply will average 105 million barrels per day in the fourth quarter, the Paris-based agency, which advises industrialized countries, said in a monthly report, 1.7 million bpd higher than forecast demand. The IEA had previously forecast a fourth-quarter supply deficit.

Iraq, OPEC's second-largest producer, has been working to find alternative export routes for its oil since the Strait of Hormuz, its usual outlet, was disrupted by the Iran war. The country has been shipping oil on hundreds of tankers to the Syrian port of Baniyas via an overland desert route which had been largely unused for decades.

In the US, President Donald Trump extended for 90 days a waiver of a shipping law to allow foreign-flagged ships to transport oil and other commodities between US ports, a White House official said on Friday.

Oil rig counts, an indicator of future supply, was unchanged at 463 this week.

  • Light Louisiana Sweet (WTC-LLS) for December delivery firmed 5 cents to a midpoint of a $1.90 premium and was seen bid and offered between a $1.80 and $2.00 a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures ​

  • Mars Sour (WTC-MRS) was unchanged at a midpoint of a $3.5 discount and was seen bid and offered between a $3.75 and $3.25 a barrel discount to U.S. crude futures ​

  • WTI Midland (WTC-WTM)was unchanged at a midpoint of a 20-cent premium and was seen bid and offered between parity and 40-cent​ a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures ​

  • West Texas Sour (WTC-WTS) was flat at a midpoint of a $3.3 discount and was seen bid and offered between a $3.50 and $3.10 a barrel discount to U.S. crude futures ​

  • WTI at East Houston (WTC-MEH), also known as MEH, traded between a 60-cent and 90-cent a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures ​

data.title: Japan Display narrows first-half net loss after restructuring
data.description:
Japan Display Inc. , the Japanese maker of small and mid-sized liquid crystal display panels, cut its net loss to JPY7.04bn ($44mn) for the six months to September, Jiji Press reported on November 13. A year earlier, the company lost JPY11.36bn over the same period.

The figures arrive months after JDI removed the threat of delisting. The panel maker had liabilities exceeding its assets at the end of March 2026. Had that position continued to the end of March 2027, the company risked breaching Tokyo Stock Exchange listing rules. JDI cleared the shortfall by the end of June. By the end of September its net assets stood at a positive JPY5bn, against a negative net worth of JPY7.41bn six months before.

Restructuring carried out in the previous fiscal year narrowed the loss, the company said. That included reducing its workforce. Paying down debt also brought interest costs lower.

Revenue moved the other way. Group sales for the half year declined 33.1% to JPY44.48bn. The company linked the decline to the end of output at its Mobara factory in Chiba Prefecture, according to results JDI published on November 12.

'Major structural reforms have reached a milestone,' JDI President Jun Akema said at a briefing on the earnings.

He said the company's attention would now turn to generating profit from the overhaul.

'Our top priority is to steadily translate these efforts into earnings and return to profitability as soon as possible,' Akema said.

data.title: Japan's Watami considers management buyout to delist
data.description:
Watami Co. , the Japanese operator of izakaya pubs, is weighing a management buyout that would take it off the stock market, Jiji Press reported on November 13, citing people with knowledge of the plan.

The company wants to give its executives more room to manoeuvre as it tries to reduce its reliance on Japanese-style pubs. Drinking is declining among consumers, and young people in particular are turning away from alcohol.

An asset management firm belonging to Miki Watanabe, who founded the restaurant group and serves as its chairman and chief executive, is expected to launch a tender offer for Watami's shares shortly, the sources said.

Watami has been building up businesses outside its pub chain. In 2024 it bought the Japanese operations of sandwich chain Subway, and it also runs boxed meal delivery services.
